data.title: Jaguar Animal Health Announces 1-for-25 Reverse Stock Split
data.description:
Jaguar Animal Health ( (JAGX) ) has provided an update.

At its November 6, 2026, special meeting, Jaguar stockholders approved an amendment authorizing a reverse split ratio from 1-for-2 to 1-for-150, with the board selecting the ratio. On November 18, Jaguar filed an amendment providing for the board-approved 1-for-25 split, then terminated it on November 19 before it took effect and filed a replacement amendment with the same terms and a November 24 effective time.

Under the replacement amendment, every 25 shares would be reclassified as one, with proportional adjustments to outstanding options, warrants and equity-plan reserves; authorized common and preferred shares would remain unchanged. On November 20, Jaguar announced the split and said it was intended to support Nasdaq listing compliance; fractional shares would be paid in cash, while street-name holders would not need to act.

data.description:

data.title: TDH Holdings Reports First-Half 2026 Financial Results
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Tdh Holdings ( (PETZ) ).

TDH Holdings, Inc., a PRC-based owner, operator and manager of commercial real estate properties, reported unaudited results for the six months ended June 30, 2026, on November 19, 2026. Revenue from continuing operations rose 26.45% to $0.74 million from $0.59 million a year earlier, as major lease renewals and a small number of new tenants increased leasing revenue.

Gross profit fell to $4,142 from $0.08 million, and gross margin declined to 0.56% from 13.31%, while operating loss widened to $0.76 million from $0.57 million; the company attributed these changes to higher leasing and operating costs. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $8.34 million, or $0.81 per share, versus net income of $1.38 million, mainly because short-term investments recorded a $7.62 million net investment loss as their fair value declined.

data.title: Vanda Reaches Settlement and License Agreement with MSN
data.description:

On November 16, 2026, Vanda entered a confidential settlement and license agreement with MSN Pharmaceuticals Inc. and MSN Laboratories Private Limited, resolving Vanda’s patent-infringement litigation in Delaware over MSN’s ANDA for a generic HETLIOZ LQ® oral suspension. Vanda granted MSN a non-exclusive, royalty-free U.S. license to manufacture, import and market the product, with the license effective in the first quarter of 2040.

MSN also received limited pre-launch manufacturing and import rights, with customer and pricing discussions allowed closer to launch, and could enter earlier under specified conditions. data.title: Erasca Reports Positive Early Data for RAS-Targeted Therapies
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Erasca ( (ERAS) ).

On November 20, 2026, Erasca announced updated U.S. Phase 1 monotherapy and initial combination data for pan-RAS molecular glue ERAS-0015 in patients with RAS-mutant solid tumors. It also announced initial U.S. Phase 1 monotherapy data for pan-KRAS inhibitor ERAS-4001, with preliminary results supporting its potential as a combination partner for ERAS-0015.

As of the September 1, 2026, data cutoff, ERAS-0015 monotherapy at 16-32 mg once daily was generally well-tolerated and showed activity across KRAS G12X cancers. Confirmed objective response rates included 44% in 25 patients with second-line-or-later pancreatic cancer, 69% in 13 patients with KRAS G12D or G12V pancreatic cancer, 58% in 12 patients with second- or third-line non-small cell lung cancer, and 75% in four biliary tract cancer patients.

At 32 mg once daily, confirmed response rates were 63% in eight KRAS G12D pancreatic cancer patients, 80% in five KRAS G12V pancreatic cancer patients, 60% in five KRAS G12D non-small cell lung cancer patients and 50% in four KRAS G12V non-small cell lung cancer patients. Safety findings remained consistent with prior 2026 disclosures, with mostly low-grade treatment-related adverse events, no dose-limiting toxicities, and no treatment discontinuations due to treatment-related adverse events at 32 mg.

Early combination testing with gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel, pembrolizumab, and panitumumab was generally well-tolerated without unexpected safety signals; responses were observed in escalation cohorts with pembrolizumab and panitumumab, while efficacy data were not yet available for the gemcitabine regimen. The company said the results supported further clinical development of ERAS-0015 combinations in pancreatic, lung and colorectal cancers.

Preliminary ERAS-4001 findings showed favorable safety and tolerability, predominantly low-grade adverse events, no treatment-related adverse events leading to discontinuation, and encouraging pharmacokinetic results. Nonclinical testing found synergistic activity for the ERAS-0015 and ERAS-4001 combination in KRAS G12X-driven models, providing a rationale for further evaluation.
